item.title: Signal Adds Protections Blocking AI Assistant Screen Access on iOS and Android
item.description:
Signal Adds Protections Blocking AI Assistant Screen Access on iOS and Android

Signal has announced new protections that block screenshots on iOS 27 and prevent AI assistants from capturing conversations on supported Android devices. These measures are designed to stop built-in AI assistants, such as Siri and Gemini, from accessing private conversation content while performing tasks for users.

🔍 Overview

The announcement follows Signal’s introduction of a feature in May 2025 that blocked Microsoft’s Recall screenshot-capturing feature on Windows 11. Signal’s president, Meredith Whittaker, stated that the company is now taking similar measures to restrict agentic systems built into iOS 17 and on Android versions where an AI assistant attempting to read the Signal screen can be detected.

Signal engineers spent months investigating how AI systems access app data. They designed targeted protections to block all extraction pathways, which were verified through reverse engineering. The protections specifically target OS-level features like Siri’s Onscreen Awareness and Google’s Gemini Intelligence, which can otherwise capture chat content as it appears on the screen.

⚙️ Key Details

The new protections operate differently across platforms:

  • iOS: The protection blocks screenshots entirely. This includes preventing users from taking screenshots of Signal conversations for legitimate purposes. On the iOS app, users can verify that “Block Siri AI” is enabled by navigating to Settings > App Security.
  • Android: Signal automatically enables Screen Security when it detects an AI assistant attempting to access the screen.
  • macOS: Signal is currently unable to provide screenshot-blocking protection for macOS. For macOS 27 users, Signal recommends adding the app to the Excluded Apps list under System Settings > Siri to prevent proactive access to message content.

Signal notes that the protections are automatically activated when possible, though specific app version numbers were not provided.

💡 Why it Matters

Signal warns that AI agents embedded deep in operating systems pose an “existential threat” because they can access conversation data through methods beyond simple screen reading. Whittaker notes that these vulnerabilities leave apps with limited options for protecting users and expose sensitive private data belonging to all conversation participants.

In response, Signal is calling on Apple, Google, and Microsoft to provide detailed documentation disclosing all potential access mechanisms. The company urges these operating system vendors to give developers a clear way to opt out of AI access across screens, files, notifications, and APIs.

#Signal #Privacy #AIAgents #Security #iOS #Android

Source: Signal to block Siri, Gemini AI from capturing chats on iOS, Android

item.title: Signal blocks screenshots on mobile to stop AI agents reading messages
item.description:
Signal blocks screenshots on mobile to stop AI agents reading messages

Signal is restricting the ability to take screenshots on Android and iOS devices to prevent AI agents from reading users’ messages and other data.

🧩 How it works

Signal is blocking Gemini and Siri AI from reading your screen. The company is addressing privacy concerns by blocking the ability to take screenshots in the app on iOS 27 and Android, which should prevent Siri, Gemini, and other Android AI assistants from reading on-screen content. Users can restore screenshot capabilities in Signal’s app settings, but the president warns that doing so will “potentially expose your (and your contacts’) Signal content to these AI agents, and break our privacy guarantees.”

⚙️ Key details

  • Limitations: The screenshot-blocking remedy is “incomplete” as it does not address alternative ways that AI agents can access app data, such as retrieving it via the device file system.
  • Platform Availability: Signal is currently unable to implement these protections on macOS.
  • Previous Precedent: Signal took a similar approach last year to prevent Microsoft’s controversial Recall feature from capturing secured chats.
  • Developer Tools: The service is struggling to develop a better solution due to the lack of available information regarding how AI agents are actually accessing application data.
  • Ecosystem Call: Signal is calling on Apple, Google, and Microsoft to provide “simple technical tools and accurate documentation” to app developers. More tools are also needed to prevent third-party agents, like Meta’s Muse, from using deep accessibility settings in apps like a “skeleton key” to access application data.

💡 Why it matters

Signal president Meredith Whittaker stated that the agentic AI capabilities built into operating systems that analyze on-screen information to learn more about the user are “undermining Signal’s ability to independently guarantee privacy.” She urged OS providers to make it easier for app developers to control what data agents can access. Whittaker emphasized: “We want to be very clear: it is a serious problem that Signal – and application developers beyond – lack robust tools to prevent AI agents from undermining application-level privacy.”

Whittaker noted that even where they are able to detect and block AI data access, major tech companies do not provide ways for developers to easily restrict such AI data access without making drastic compromises to the core user experience. She concluded: “We all need to recognize that the current integration of AI agents into the operating system, without these common-sense remedies, represents an existential threat to privacy at the application layer, and the ability of independent developers like Signal to protect your sensitive data,” adding that “Signal is the canary in the coal mine, but this affects the entire ecosystem and should galvanize anyone who cares about these fundamental rights.”

#Signal #AIAgents #Privacy #iOS27 #Android

Source: Signal is blocking Gemini and Siri AI from reading your screen
